title: Proteomics Market Size, Share & Forecast 2026-2032

market_overview.summary: Published proteomics market estimates agree unusually well — $31.0 billion to $41.97 billion for 2025, a spread of only 1.35x — and that agreement is misleading rather than reassuring. All of them are counting protein-related laboratory and service spend, and one publisher defines its consumables category to include buffers, chromatography columns and electrophoresis gels. We publish the narrowest stated scope, BCC Research's: $35.03 billion in 2026 rising to $72.93 billion by 2032 at 13.0%. The finding is the gap underneath it. The entire disclosed FY2025 revenue of the next-generation proteomics platform sector — Quanterix, SomaLogic, Standard BioTools and Seer combined — is $340.5 million, which is 0.83% of a $41.2 billion published headline. A reader who treats the headline as an addressable market for a proteomics platform is out by roughly 100x.
key_trends: Affinity proteomics has consolidated into sequencing companies: Illumina agreed to buy SomaLogic for $350 million cash plus up to $75 million in milestones (announced 23 June 2025, completed 30 January 2026), and Olink already sits inside Thermo Fisher

The pure-play sector is tiny relative to its publicity: Quanterix $138.9 million, SomaLogic approximately $99.7 million, Standard BioTools $85.3 million and Seer $16.6 million in FY2025 — $340.5 million in total

Mass spectrometry remains the technical centre of gravity but is reported inside diversified instrument segments: Thermo Fisher's Analytical Instruments was $7.55 billion and Bruker's BSI CALID $1.21 billion in FY2025, neither with a proteomics split
Instrument demand is flat to down: Thermo Fisher's Analytical Instruments segment grew 1% reported and was flat organically in FY2025, and Bruker's whole company declined 4% organically
Plasma proteomics for biomarker discovery is the application pulling platform adoption, which is why the acquirers are sequencing and diagnostics companies rather than instrument makers

Regulatory demand is arriving from an unexpected direction: FDA's 10 April 2025 roadmap encourages new approach methodologies in investigational new drug applications, which makes proteomic safety readouts a submission-relevant rather than purely exploratory measurement
market_overview.adoption_level: Ubiquitous as a method, early as a platform market

drivers: Plasma and tissue biomarker discovery in drug development, which is the application that justifies high-plex platform purchases rather than incremental mass-spectrometry capacity

A very wide consumables base: antibodies, assay kits, protein chips, buffers, chromatography columns and electrophoresis gels are recurring purchases independent of platform cycles, and are what makes the published market large
Multiomics bundling by sequencing companies, with Illumina acquiring SomaLogic and Thermo Fisher holding Olink — proteomic content sold alongside genomic content to the same customer

FDA's April 2025 new approach methodologies roadmap, which encourages non-animal, human-relevant data including molecular safety readouts in IND submissions and gives proteomic assays a regulatory use case
Falling cost per protein measured as high-plex affinity panels compete with mass spectrometry on depth-per-dollar rather than on absolute coverage
restraints: The addressable platform market is roughly 100x smaller than the published headline: $340.5 million of disclosed pure-play revenue against a $41.2 billion published total, which has repeatedly led investors and entrants to misjudge the opportunity

Instrument capital spend is flat: Thermo Fisher's Analytical Instruments segment was flat organically in FY2025 and Bruker declined 4% organically, both on academic, government and biopharma budget pressure

Pure-play economics are poor at current scale — Seer reported FY2025 revenue of $16.6 million against operating expenses of $86.5 million, and Standard BioTools has been cutting over $40 million of annualised costs to reach positive adjusted EBITDA
No reimbursement for proteomic profiling: with narrow exceptions there is no CPT-coded, payer-funded proteomic test, so clinical volume cannot underwrite platform growth

Reference-standard and reproducibility problems: affinity and mass-spectrometry platforms do not produce interchangeable protein quantities, which slows the standardisation clinical adoption would require
opportunities: Clinical proteomic testing under CLIA, a route made cheaper by the March 2025 vacatur of FDA's laboratory-developed tests rule — SomaLogic's Boulder site is already CLIA- and CAP-certified
Regulatory-grade safety and toxicology readouts under FDA's new approach methodologies programme, which converts exploratory proteomics into submission-supporting data
Population-scale plasma proteomics attached to biobank cohorts, where a single customer buys hundreds of thousands of assays and changes a platform company's revenue scale in one contract

Consolidation at low valuations: Illumina paid $350 million cash for SomaLogic, roughly equal to the whole pure-play sector's disclosed annual revenue, which sets a cheap benchmark for further acquisition
Proteogenomics — pairing proteomic readouts with existing genomic data — where the incremental sale is content on an installed sequencing base rather than new capital equipment
challenges: The published market measures activity, not an addressable market, and no publisher says so: one house's consumables definition includes buffers and gels, which is why its total reaches 92.5% of Thermo Fisher's entire company revenue

One publisher's proteomics instruments line alone, $8.0 billion for 2025, exceeds the $7.55 billion FY2025 revenue of Thermo Fisher's whole Analytical Instruments segment, a business spanning chromatography, microscopy and chemical analysis across every application
Disclosure is disappearing as the sector consolidates: Olink inside Thermo Fisher's Life Sciences Solutions, SomaLogic inside Illumina, Akoya inside Quanterix — none separately reported
Platform companies compete against incumbent mass spectrometry that customers already own and have already paid for, so the sale is a displacement rather than an addition

Scope dependence is extreme: BCC's explicit exclusion of protein structural analysis and protein-expression products accounts for much of the $10 billion gap between its 2025 figure and the next house's

regulatory_landscape: No FDA marketing pathway applies to the bulk of proteomics products, which are sold research-use-only. The exception is a clinical proteomic test, which must either obtain device authorisation or be offered as a laboratory-developed test.

Clinical Laboratory Improvement Amendments (CLIA), administered by CMS, with CAP accreditation as the practical additional requirement: this is the operative regime for clinical proteomic testing, and SomaLogic's Boulder facility holds both certifications.

FDA's laboratory-developed tests final rule was vacated in its entirety by U.S. District Judge Sean D. Jordan on 31 March 2025, on the ground that LDTs are not devices under the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act and that Congress assigned oversight to CMS under CLIA. FDA did not appeal within the 60-day window.

FDA's Biomarker Qualification Program, operating under section 507 of the Food and Drug Administration Safety and Innovation Act framework as extended by the 21st Century Cures Act, is the route by which a proteomic biomarker becomes usable across multiple drug development programmes without re-justification in each IND.

FDA's 10 April 2025 roadmap on phasing out animal testing requirements for monoclonal antibodies and other drugs encourages new approach methodologies, including molecular and in-silico toxicity readouts, in investigational new drug applications. It encourages rather than requires their use, and it does not qualify any specific proteomic assay.
EU In Vitro Diagnostic Regulation 2017/746 governs any proteomic product placed on the EU market for a diagnostic purpose, with conformity assessment obligations scaling by risk class.

research_methodology.data_validation: The headline is one publisher's own base advanced at its own rate, labelled as interpolation: BCC Research's $31.0 billion for 2025 becomes $35.03 billion for 2026 and $72.93 billion for 2032 at 13.0%. The internal check is that the modelled 2030 point, $57.12 billion, sits 0.14% from BCC's separately published $57.2 billion for 2030. BCC was chosen because it publishes the narrowest stated scope and is the only house in the set to publish an explicit exclusion list (protein structural analysis and protein-expression products are out of scope), which makes it the most checkable, and because it carries the lowest base among dated full-scope series. Three grounding calculations were run against audited and reported FY2025 revenue. First, one publisher's proteomics instruments line of $8.0 billion for 2025 is 1.06x Thermo Fisher Scientific's entire Analytical Instruments segment revenue of $7.55 billion, a business spanning chromatography, mass spectrometry, microscopy and chemical analysis across all applications. Second, that publisher's $41.2 billion total is 3.75x the combined $10.99 billion of Thermo Fisher's Analytical Instruments segment and the whole of Bruker, and 92.5% of Thermo Fisher's entire $44.56 billion company revenue. Third, the summed disclosed FY2025 revenue of the next-generation proteomics platform sector — Quanterix $138.9 million, SomaLogic approximately $99.7 million derived as the difference between Standard BioTools' preliminary combined-company revenue of about $185 million and its $85.3 million of continuing operations, Standard BioTools continuing $85.3 million, and Seer $16.6 million — is $340.5 million, or 0.83% of the $41.2 billion headline, a factor of 121. Illumina's $350 million cash price for SomaLogic is roughly equal to that whole sum. These are scope and plausibility tests, not market estimates: they establish that the published figures measure protein-related laboratory and service spend rather than a purchasable platform market, and they do not establish the correct figure for either reading. The SomaLogic line is our own subtraction between two of one company's disclosures; Olink, Nautilus, Bruker's proteomics line and all private vendors sit outside the $340.5 million sum, so it is a floor. Regional, country and segment shares are published as empty or as plain strings because the only source offering them presents no method, and no vendor market share is published because none is disclosed.

faqs.question: How large is the proteomics market?
faqs.answer: We publish $35.03 billion for 2026, rising to $72.93 billion by 2032 at 13.0%, derived from BCC Research's published $31.0 billion for 2025 and its own 13.0% rate. Published 2025 estimates run from $31.0 billion to $41.97 billion — a narrow 1.35x spread. The important qualification is what that figure counts: protein-related instruments, services and a consumables category that one publisher defines to include buffers, chromatography columns and electrophoresis gels.

faqs.question: Why do the publishers agree with each other here when they disagree elsewhere?
faqs.answer: Because they are all doing the same sum. Each adds up protein-related laboratory and service spend across pharma, academia and diagnostics. Agreeing on the answer to the same wide question is not the same as the question being the right one. None of them sizes the next-generation proteomics platform market separately, and that is the market the sector's investment narrative concerns.

faqs.question: How big is the addressable market for a proteomics platform company?
faqs.answer: Far smaller than the headline. The entire disclosed FY2025 revenue of the publicly reporting pure-play sector — Quanterix $138.9 million, SomaLogic approximately $99.7 million, Standard BioTools continuing operations $85.3 million and Seer $16.6 million — is $340.5 million. That is 0.83% of a $41.2 billion published total, a factor of 121. The figure is a floor, since Olink, Bruker's proteomics line and private vendors are not in it, but it would have to be wrong by two orders of magnitude for the published totals to be describing the same thing.

faqs.question: Can the $41 billion figure be checked against anything?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it does not survive. That publisher puts proteomics instruments alone at $8.0 billion for 2025. Thermo Fisher Scientific's entire Analytical Instruments segment — chromatography, mass spectrometry, electron microscopy and chemical analysis, sold into pharma, academia, semiconductors, forensics and environmental testing — was $7.55 billion in FY2025. The proteomics instrument line is being valued at more than the whole instrument business of the world's largest analytical-instrument company, in which proteomics is a minority application.

faqs.question: What does Illumina's purchase of SomaLogic tell us about the market's size?
faqs.answer: A great deal. Illumina paid $350 million in cash plus up to $75 million in milestones for one of the two leading affinity-proteomics platforms, with the deal announced in June 2025 and completed on 30 January 2026. The cash consideration is roughly equal to the entire disclosed annual revenue of the pure-play proteomics sector, and 0.85% of a $41.2 billion published market. Acquirers price what they can sell, not what the market reports say exists.

faqs.question: Which company leads proteomics?
faqs.answer: Thermo Fisher Scientific, by a wide margin, through mass spectrometry and the Olink affinity platform — but it discloses no proteomics split, so no share can be stated and we assign none. Among independents, Bruker's timsTOF line competes in mass spectrometry (inside a $1.21 billion BSI CALID segment) and Quanterix is the largest disclosing pure-play at $138.9 million of FY2025 revenue.

faqs.question: What would make proteomics grow faster than 13%?
faqs.answer: Three identifiable things, none of them an extrapolation. Population-scale plasma proteomics on biobank cohorts, where one contract changes a platform company's revenue scale. Reimbursed clinical proteomic testing, which barely exists today and which the March 2025 vacatur of FDA's laboratory-developed test rule makes cheaper to pursue but does not fund. And regulatory adoption of proteomic safety readouts under FDA's April 2025 new approach methodologies roadmap, which encourages but does not require their use in IND submissions.

seo.meta_title: Proteomics Market Size, Share & Forecast to 2032
seo.meta_description: Proteomics market at $35.03B in 2026, reaching $72.93B by 2032 at 13.0% — and why the disclosed pure-play platform sector is 121x smaller than the headline.

executive_summary: Proteomics is the market in this corpus where the publishers agree and are collectively measuring the wrong thing. Estimates for 2025 run from BCC Research's $31.0 billion to $41.97 billion — a spread of only 1.35x, and published CAGRs cluster between 12.0% and 16.55%. We publish BCC's series, the narrowest stated scope and the only one with an explicit exclusion list: $35.03 billion in 2026 to $72.93 billion by 2032 at 13.0%, interpolated from BCC's own base and rate and checked against BCC's own 2030 figure to within 0.14%. What the agreement conceals is visible the moment the totals meet audited revenue. One publisher puts proteomics instruments alone at $8.0 billion for 2025; Thermo Fisher Scientific's entire Analytical Instruments segment, spanning chromatography, mass spectrometry, microscopy and chemical analysis across every application, was $7.55 billion in FY2025. The same publisher's $41.2 billion total is 3.75x the combined revenue of that segment and the whole of Bruker, and 92.5% of Thermo Fisher's entire company. Meanwhile the whole disclosed revenue of the next-generation proteomics platform sector — Quanterix, SomaLogic, Standard BioTools and Seer — is $340.5 million, or 0.83% of the headline. Illumina's cash price for SomaLogic, $350 million, is roughly the whole of it. The published figures are a measure of how much protein work the world does, including buffers and gels. They are not an addressable market, and nobody writing them says so.
key_highlights: Headline: $35.03 billion in 2026 to $72.93 billion in 2032 at 13.0%, interpolated from BCC Research's own published 2025 base and rate
Published 2025 estimates span only 1.35x ($31.0B-$41.97B) — agreement that reflects a shared method, not a measured market
One publisher's proteomics instruments line, $8.0 billion for 2025, exceeds Thermo Fisher's entire $7.55 billion Analytical Instruments segment across all applications
That publisher's $41.2 billion total is 3.75x Thermo Fisher Analytical Instruments plus the whole of Bruker, and 92.5% of Thermo Fisher's entire $44.56 billion company revenue
Disclosed FY2025 revenue of the pure-play platform sector is $340.5 million — 0.83% of the headline, a factor of 121
Illumina paid $350 million cash for SomaLogic, roughly equal to the entire disclosed revenue of that sector
One publisher's consumables category, 69.4% of its total, is defined to include buffers, chromatography columns and electrophoresis gels
market_context: Proteomics has two meanings and one market size, which is the source of nearly every error made about it. In the first meaning, proteomics is what laboratories do to proteins: run them on gels, separate them on columns, quantify them with antibodies, identify them on mass spectrometers. On that reading a $31-41 billion global figure is defensible, because it is counting a very large base of recurring laboratory supplies and services — and one publisher says so explicitly, defining its consumables category to include buffers and electrophoresis gels. In the second meaning, proteomics is a class of new high-plex platforms intended to do for proteins what sequencing did for nucleic acids. That is what the sector's venture funding, its acquisitions and its press releases are about, and it is measurable: $340.5 million of disclosed FY2025 revenue across Quanterix, SomaLogic, Standard BioTools and Seer. The two readings differ by about 100x. The supplier structure reinforces the point: the companies that actually hold the revenue — Thermo Fisher, Bruker, Danaher, Agilent — report proteomics nowhere, because for them it is an application of instruments sold into many markets. The companies that are proteomics report revenue in the tens of millions.
forecast_analysis: Our 13.0% is the bottom of the published range, applied to the lowest dated full-scope base, and the resulting series reproduces BCC Research's own 2030 figure to within 0.14% — so it is faithful to its source. Whether it is a useful forecast depends entirely on which market the reader has in mind. For protein-related tools and consumables spend, 13.0% is a claim that a very broad laboratory-supply base compounds at roughly twice nominal GDP, in a period when the largest supplier's instrument segment grew 1% reported and was flat organically, and the second-largest declined 4% organically. That is a forecast about recovering research budgets and about consumables pull-through, and it is the same bet the single-cell and spatial forecasts make. For the platform sector, the published rate is close to meaningless: a 13% rate on a $340.5 million disclosed base gives $728 million by 2032, which is a different report. The two identifiable things that could break the pattern are both step changes rather than rates — population-scale plasma proteomics contracts attached to biobank cohorts, and regulatory uptake of proteomic readouts under FDA's April 2025 new approach methodologies roadmap, which encourages their inclusion in IND submissions without requiring it or qualifying any specific assay. Readers should hold the two numbers separately and never apply a published CAGR across the boundary.
reader_takeaways: Decide which proteomics you mean before quoting a size. Protein-related tools and consumables spend is $31-42 billion; the disclosed next-generation platform sector is $340.5 million. The gap is about 100x and no published report flags it.

Test any proteomics headline against instrument-company revenue. A $41.2 billion market implies an instruments line larger than Thermo Fisher's entire Analytical Instruments segment, which covers far more than proteomics.
Read the consumables definition. When buffers, chromatography columns and electrophoresis gels are inside it, the total is measuring laboratory activity, not a platform opportunity.
Use the acquisition prices as the reality check. Illumina paid $350 million in cash for SomaLogic — roughly the whole pure-play sector's annual revenue, and under 1% of the published market.
Expect the sector to keep consolidating into sequencing and diagnostics companies, which also means the public disclosure this analysis depends on will keep shrinking.
